title: Quick and hard bodyweight calf exercise for hypertrophy
summary: Shows a quick bodyweight calf raise done standing on the lowest setting of a power rack, letting bodyweight stretch the calves at the bottom and squeezing at the top. Less hand support makes it harder; high reps to failure, bending the knee briefly to recover. Start with 2 sets of 25-30 full-ROM reps.

claims.claim: For a quick calf workout with only a rack, stand on the lowest rack setting with the front of the foot on it and do calf raises; don't do it on round bars, which are unstable and dangerous.
Let bodyweight stretch the calves at the bottom, then extend up and squeeze at the top; experiment with foot position and angle.
Holding the rack with fewer fingers, one hand, or less force puts more load on the calves; 30-40 reps produce a strong burn.
Heavy, unfit people should be careful: the exercise stretches the Achilles tendon, and a snapped Achilles requires surgery.
When the calves tire, bend at the knee briefly to let them recover, then keep going to failure.
Start with only 2 sets of 25-30 full-ROM reps and adjust volume based on how the calves feel the next day.
He is adding this to his calf routine with the goal of reaching 18-inch calves and beyond.

exercises.name: Bodyweight calf raise on rack
cues: stand on lowest rack setting, not round bars
let bodyweight stretch at the bottom
